The sky over Haldor Prime was a churning mass of storm clouds and bio-ships, blotting out the sun and casting the battlefield in an eerie twilight. Private Marcus Hale gripped his lasgun, sweat mixing with the grime on his forehead. Around him, the remnants of his regiment stood trembling, eyes fixed on the horizon where a seething tide of Tyranids advanced, their chittering screams piercing the air.

"Steady! Hold your ground!" the lieutenant barked, but his voice wavered. Marcus swallowed hard, his mouth dry as ash. The ground shook with the approach of countless alien monstrosities—Hormagaunts, Termagants, and worse.

A distant roar grew louder, a sound not of alien origin but of engines and faith. Marcus turned to see Thunderhawk gunships streaking across the sky, emblazoned with the sigil of the Ultramarines. The aircraft unleashed a barrage of missiles before deploying their cargo: Space Marines in azure armor descending on jump packs, landing with thunderous impact.

"For the Emperor!" the leading Space Marine shouted, his power sword crackling with energy. The sight ignited a spark of hope in Marcus's chest.

The Space Marines charged, meeting the Tyranid swarm head-on. Bolters thundered, each explosive round tearing through alien flesh. A Space Marine paused beside Marcus, his armor scarred but imposing.

"Guardsman, fall in behind us. We will purge this xenos filth," he commanded through his helmet's vox grille.

"Yes, sir!" Marcus replied, his voice steadying. He took position, firing his lasgun at the approaching swarm. The Tyranids were relentless, but the combined might of the Imperial Guard and the Adeptus Astartes held them at bay.

A Lictor burst from the shadows, its claws poised to strike. Marcus barely had time to react when the Space Marine beside him intercepted the creature, their weapons clashing in a shower of sparks. With a swift strike, the Marine cleaved the Lictor in two.

"Stay vigilant," the Space Marine warned. "They come from all directions."

The battle raged on. Bioplasma seared the ground, and spores filled the air with toxic miasma. Yet, amidst the chaos, Marcus found himself fighting with a fervor he didn't know he possessed. The presence of the Space Marines was a bulwark against despair.

An ear-splitting roar announced the arrival of a Carnifex, its massive form barreling toward their lines. "Concentrate fire!" the lieutenant ordered. Lasgun beams converged on the beast, but it hardly slowed.

The Ultramarine sergeant raised his power fist. "With me, brothers!" He and his squad charged the Carnifex, engaging it in a brutal melee. Marcus watched in awe as they brought the creature down, their unity and strength turning the tide.

As the last of the Tyranids fell or retreated, a hush settled over the battlefield. The ground was littered with the remnants of the xenos swarm. The surviving Guardsmen looked around, disbelief and relief etched on their faces.

The Space Marine sergeant approached Marcus. "You fought well, Guardsman. The Emperor smiles upon your courage."

"Thank you, sir," Marcus said, standing a little taller.

The sergeant nodded before moving on, his duty calling him elsewhere. The storm clouds began to part, revealing a sliver of blue sky.

Marcus took a deep breath, the air heavy but alive with the scent of victory. He glanced at his fellow soldiers, their expressions mirroring his own mix of exhaustion and renewed hope.

"The Emperor protects," he whispered, his faith restored.

Its a good game. Is it the best game? No. Is it revolutionary? No. Does it bring brand new ideas to the table? No. Is it fun? Oh hell yes it is. Ever wanted to feel like a god on the battlefield cutting through enemies? This is your game, just play the campaign on the first difficulty. Want a challenging experience in line with 40K lore? Play the game on the third difficulty. Its just a good game. Price to fun ratio through the roof.

UPDATE: I am flipping my review to negative because for the last 6 months I have been unable to finish a SINGLE SESSION without the game crashing. I have done EVERYTHING to resolve these crashes and nothing works, and it's only this game that crashes. So it's a no from me, now.

[h1] The Big Picture [/h1]

Much like its genetically modified super soldier protagonists, Space Marine 2's one and only identity is combat. In the grim darkness of the far future, there is only war, and few games distill the grim dark essence of Warhammer 40k quite like Space Marine 2. That's simply not enough for some gamers, and that's fine. But if you just want to experience some of the most stoic, bombastic, and brutal combat in recent gaming with your battle brothers, or want to see the greatest visual portrayal of the 40k universe to date; this game is a must-buy.

[h1] This Combat System Rules [/h1]

Hiding behind the veil of familiar souls-like mechanics is a surprisingly unfamiliar combat system that actually inherits more from DOOM 2016's "push forward" combat philosphy than anything. They've taken the idea of DOOM's glory kills and made it the center piece of the combat system. Using the swarm engine to render hundreds of enemies on screen at once, there is simply too much incoming damage and enemy actions to keep up with. That's why they've created a parry, dodge, and execute system that is loaded with bespoke animations, armor recovery, i-frames, and AOE stuns. Running and kiting enemies is suicide. There is an emphasis on active defense. The only way to survive is put yourself in the thick of things and get as many parries and executes as possible, each one stunning surrounding enemies and refilling your armor, giving you just enough of a window to be aggressive and trigger the next one. If you can chain these back to back, you experience a brilliant flow-state that few games achieve. The most threatening enemies are not the ones that do the most damage, but rather the ones that have the ability to knock you out of this flow state that prevents you from taking damage. There is also a system called "contested health" which allows you restore any damage you've taken in the past 2 seconds, rewarding players for pushing through incoming damage to reach that next execute and regain their flow. While there's some balance issues with some enemy types that are a little bit too much of a burden on this delicate action economy, the core is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic, but it requires you to abandon some of those souls-like instincts you've spent the past few years building up.

[h1] If 2 of the 3 game modes hit for you, that's enough for the game to be worth it. [/h1]

 The campaign is a short 6-8 hours but with zero filler and non-stop epic moments and incredible set pieces and presentation. The campaign can be played completely offline, but it can also be played in coop. While there's been a lot of complaints about the bots being useless (they basically do nothing except revive you when you go down), every difficulty of this game is soloable and I've solo'd normal, veteran, and most of the hardest difficulty at the time of writing. If you like macho heroism even the slightest bit, this campaign will make you nerd out frequently.

The PvP: I'll be honest, I haven't played it, because I didn't buy the game for that. I'm fine with that. You can read other reviews about the PvP.

The star of the show, and what I think represents the true potential longevity of the mode, is the coop operations. The difficulty scaling for these is very different from the campaign. Rather than making the mechanics more difficult, the operations set a baseline for mechanical operations and scale the player power and enemy power together. The 6 classes actually have a lot more depth than I expected, I've played all 6 up to the 3rd of 4 difficulties and 2 of them all the way to end game at the point of writing. Where the campaign offers no player progression or customization in favor of a super tight experience, Operations classes have impactful perk trees, very good visual customization (no mtx), and the most shocking of all, a surprisingly deep subset of weapons to progress. Each weapon not only has its own (slim) perk tree, but also has several sub-variants that tend to have a pretty big impact on how they actually play. While some are relatively simple changes like focuses on damage versus ammo reserve, some behave completely differently from their baseline variants, like the grenade launcher variant of the bolt rifle or the marksman variant of the bolt carbine. Melee weapons are the stand out becase each variant has different animation speeds, swing sizes, and parry window timings, which has a profound difference on the flow of combat once you understand the game at a high level. The perk trees do a lot to evolve the gameplay as well. The big issue with operations is balance. There are several weapon types that are just straight up bad and not worth using, ever. There's also many perk lines that have 1 very clear and obvious "win the game" perk while the other options you would never use in a million years. This means that perk tree diversity is deperessingly linear for all of the 6 classes. You get some variance based on what weapons people run, but perk balance is currently terrible.

[h1] Matchmaking Sucks [/h1]

My biggest issue with the game in its current state besides some pretty bad balance is the matchmaking. Matches have restrictions blocking mutliple players from queueing up as the same class, however the matchmaker doesn't care about this distinction and is matchmaking people into invalid game states where they can't even start or enter the game they matchmade into. The Matchmaker also seems to frequently break, where it simply won't match you with anything at all, despite a hundred thousand players being active concurrently on PC alone and crossplay enabled. Trying to matchmake is a constant wrench in the experience. There's also been occassional rollbacks where players have lost a session's worth of progress to a server rollback. This hasn't actually affected me once in my hundred hours but it's happening. There's also rumors of people being completely unable to connect to the servers, but that's also never once affected me or any of my 2 battle brothers.

[h1] Future Content is coming [/h1]

First major patch is tomorrow (Sep. 26) which should bring some baseline improvements to the game, but the highlights of the current roadmap include new operations enemies and missions later in the year, a horde mode mid 2025, and there's even talk that the game has succeeded enough to pivot Saber development towards producing formerly unplanned paid DLC story expansions. If I'm being honest, this is the best opencritic 82 game I can think of playing, but I also recognize I'm well within the game's target audience. For me personally this game is a low 90s type of game.

If you like Warhammer 40k and want a game that scratches the lore itch, this is it. 

Main campaign is kind of short, but there is a significant amount of PVP and PVE content that will hopefully be expanded upon in future updates. 

Voice acting is mostly good, a few lines fall flat but that's to be expected. 
Graphics are great, lots of details and lore in every nook and cranny. 
Animations can get a bit repetitive, especially as important as the Execution function is. 
Weapons are mostly fun in campaign. 
Upgrade system in multiplayer is based on actually playing the game, the only paid dlc is for cosmetics. 
Moving from single player to multiplayer is easy to do, highly recommend doing the challenges for each class to understand the mechanics and how things differ between single and multiplayer equipment (JUMP-PACKS). 
There are some moments where the action starts to feel a little stale. It's hard to get tired of someone screaming "FOR THE EMPORAHHHH" and smashing a hammer into xeno's skull but when you see it for the 50th time... in a row...
Wonderful. Hoping for more single player/co-op content in the future!

Concerned only with campaign, which exposes the issues I have with the game's core design philosophy.

TLDR: You're now playing as 3 Marines, and it feels like the overall durability, speed, and power has been divided by 3 so that each individual marine in the squad is made of paper compared to the first game. This feels terrible if you aren't constantly drunk and playing with friends on voice chat on the easier difficulties. 

Game says Veteran is intended difficulty. Okay, let's go. I played the first one on higher difficulties.

You're ostensibly fighting swarm enemies. Cool, sword for chaff, gun for everything else right?

Nah. You now have much more limited actual health regeneration and enemies chunk you for damage while backing up to deal with the swarm. You get shot constantly and can't heal it off. So just take cover and peek to shoot?

Nah. They have more angles on you, more health, no ammunition concerns, and will whittle you down assuming you didn't already deal with the melee units. So go unga bunga and charge the ranged units and tie them up right?

Nah. You'll get shredded trying to close with a stumpy little sprint. The first game's fury doesn't offset this at all. And even if you do close with the ranged units, they still fire at you and aren't guaranteed to flinch if you start swinging. 

Can you eventually persevere and win? Sure. In the same way that you can eventually "persevere" through slamming your hand between a doorframe until it finally falls off.

Battle-Brothers, I have been tasked with following our Primarch's glorious example in writing a treatise on how to combat the vile xenos Tyranids. 

The Tyranid swarm is vast, and its collective conciseness is not above using the lives of its drones to expend your ammunition, leaving you vulnerable. Fortunately, we are Astartes and may use our blades to exterminate the xenos scum in vast numbers. But beware, many Tyranid bio-forms specialize in close combat, and so melee will be a dance of death, but we are the Angels of Death and We Shall Know No Fear.

When smaller bio-forms [b][Target:Minoris/Hormegaunt][/b] attack, it is most expedient to dispatch the enemy with light quick attacks of your melee weapon [b][Tap melee attack button][/b]. If the enemy telegraphs its attack [b][Blue cresent][/b], be prepared and make it suffer [b][Hold the parry button to counter the strike][/b]. If a larger beast [b][Target:Majoris/Warrior][/b] attacks, a quick and well timed parry [b][Tap parry button, timing is important!][/b] will leave it open to counter attacks. If the enemy fights defensively [b][Blocks][/b], use heavy strikes to shatter their guard [b][Hold melee attack button][/b]. If the xenos use a heavy attack of their own [b][Red crescent][/b], it is best to dodge out of the way [b][Tap dodge button][/b] so as to not compromise armor integrity [b][Take damage][/b], this can also disorient the foe, who cannot fathom our agility.

Ammunition should be used sparingly, and whenever possible, used on high value targets and ranged enemies that can not be easily reached. An observant mind may find ways not to waste shots [b][Shoot explosives to eliminate multiple enemies][/b], and a steady hand will conserve ammunition [b][Headshots deal increased damage][/b]. While it may seem prudent to fire your holy boltgun at maximum rate against the endless swarm, remember your bolter drills and be like the Sons of Dorn [b][Fire in short bursts to control recoil][/b]. A disoriented enemy [b][Red crosshair][/b] can be easily dispatched with a well placed shot from your sidearm [b][Tap the shoot button without aiming][/b], such an attack needs not worry about ammunition for the Emperor provides [b][Gun-strikes do not use ammo][/b].

Severe damage may stun the foe [b][Red outline][/b] where they may be easily executed [b][Tap the finisher button][/b]. It is reinvigorating tearing the xenos apart [b][Executing enemies restores armor and restores recoverable health][/b], and even the alien mind can not help but be humbled by such a show of Imperial might [b][You are invulnerable while performing a finisher][/b]. The synaptic feedback from eliminating larger bio-forms can kill or incapacitate lesser Tyranids.

Heed these words and turn these theatricals into practicals. Fight well Brothers, I look forward to serving alongside you on the front lines.
